scope: Theorem 2.10 (Pure Dobrushin interface) of the manuscript “SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions” (preprints/SLE3-universality-for-weak-finite-range-Ising-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 44a7837e35328259), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In ordinary lattice approximations of a fixed polygonal Jordan domain with two distinct marked boundary points, the critical nearest-neighbor Ising interface with opposite constant signs on the two marked arcs converges to chordal SLE3. Convergence is in uniform distance modulo increasing reparametrization, oriented from the first mark to the second. Either local turn at an alternating face is allowed, including the deterministic rule of the problem. Bounded local rounding and half-stubs have vanishing effect on this convergence.
